purpose: A single-run ratio against a baseline resolves nothing below that baseline's own run-to-run spread. This records the spread beside the baseline so a comparison has to say which side of the noise it falls on.

overall_spread.statement: measured over 2 runs and 106 configs; a single-run ratio against v6-anchor cannot resolve anything inside [0.9408, 1.235]

memory.statement: measured over 2 runs and 90 configs; a single-run ratio against v6-anchor:memory cannot resolve anything inside [0.9367, 1.2253]

reduce.statement: measured over 2 runs and 8 configs; a single-run ratio against v6-anchor:reduce cannot resolve anything inside [1.017, 1.491]

gemm.statement: measured over 2 runs and 8 configs; a single-run ratio against v6-anchor:gemm cannot resolve anything inside [1.0062, 1.0443]

cross_check_against_committed_probe.note: AFTER the 6.6.7 rework the module computes the SAME statistic the probe does -- signed, baseline-relative v_later/v_baseline per config -- so these now agree exactly rather than approximately. An earlier version used a max/median statistic, could not represent the fast side, and disagreed here; that is what the reviewer caught.
